result.title: Scalable Counterfactual Explanations for Time Series via Policy Learning
result.summary: Generating counterfactual (CF) explanations for time series is challenging due to complex temporal dependencies and the computational inefficiency of traditional instance-specific optimization. We propose a policy learning framework for counterfactual explanation in time series, trained as a one-step contextual-bandit policy-learning problem. By training an actor-critic agent in the latent space of a pre-trained autoencoder, our method learns a transferable policy that captures global structural regularities. Unlike existing methods that rely on iterative optimization for each new input, the learned policy enables direct generation of valid and plausible counterfactuals through a single forward pass, avoiding per-instance optimization at inference time. Experiments on 13 UCR benchmark datasets show that our framework achieves high validity and strong plausibility across multiple anomaly detection metrics. Overall, by decoupling counterfactual generation from per-instance optimization, the proposed method provides an efficient and scalable alternative to existing approaches for time series counterfactual explanations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出面向时间序列反事实解释的策略学习框架：在预训练自编码器的隐空间中用 actor-critic 训练一次性的 contextual bandit 策略，使其在推理时单次前向即生成有效且合理的反事实，免去逐实例迭代优化，并在 13 个 UCR 数据集上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「隐空间中学习可迁移策略、单次前向替代逐实例优化」的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的生成与训练监督提供借鉴；但任务是时间序列反事实生成，与视觉推理无直接联系，需核查策略输出是否依赖具体证据而非仅学得全局先验。
